Digital 2027 Nissan Z Shooting Brake Comes Packing With a Widebody Kit and Big-Lipped Copper Wheels
7 photos
Photo: kelsonik / Instagram
The Japanese automaker Nissan has had many novelties for automotive enthusiasts over the past few weeks, including for a few of its most important regions like Australia or North America.
Last month, Mitsubishi announced the pricing of its new Eclipse Sportback, and Nissan dropped laughing because the EV is around $8k more than its Leaf despite the obvious sharing of major hardware. Nissan also had Nismo open its first performance center outside the home market of Japan all the way in the Land Down Under, while Mexico got a taste of the new Frontier Pro with both ICE and plug-in hybrid powertrains, and Nissan announced that its US deliveries have gone up for almost 20 uninterrupted months thanks to carried momentum by the Rogue, Frontier, and the new Armada.
Surprisingly, the automaker also revealed a few weeks ago that its Altima is not biting the dust like other passenger cars for the 2027 model year – though it does cost more, of course. Last but not least, the 2027 Nissan Pathfinder got a retro throwback to its roots from 1987 through new special edition models adding extra comfort creatures.
Anyway, that’s all the news about Nissan from the past month, condensed – and, unfortunately, it doesn’t say anything about the 2027 Nissan Z, the company’s last surviving sports car on the US automotive market. The latest model year is offered both in the US and Canada , where it’s also much cheaper, by the way, with several enhancements, including the addition of a six-speed manual transmission for the Nismo version.
The 2027 Nissan Z also gained some features from the defunct R25 Nissan GT-R to make it even more capable both on the street and at the local track, as well as various subtle changes compared to the previous model years, including a new Shinkai Green Pearl Metallic exterior color which can be combined with the Z Performance’s new tan interior upholstery option to make it vintage cool.
Anyway, a member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators has decided to stop dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI and make it far more enticing with a brand-new body style. More precisely, Nikita Chuicko, the virtual artist better known as " kelsonik " on social media, thinks that now is the right CGI time to work on the 2027 Nissan Z with an unofficial, hypothetical Shooting Brake design project.
It’s not just more practical thanks to the added space behind the seats, but it also has a decidedly Japanese flavor thanks to the combination of a striking yellow paint and the gloss black roof mixed with a JDM-style widebody fender flare kit and the new copper-hue big-lipped alloy wheels. So, what do you think – yay or nay? View this post on Instagram A post shared by CAR DESIGN | RENDERINGS (@kelsonik)
